note: A faithful rendering of the Vinaya case narratives on bowls and teaching postures; the rule formulas and the six monks' episodes are all correctly handled.

errors.english: The entities of the aggregates, which are the coming and going of unlearned misconceptions, are what are dependent or caused.
errors.why: The Tibetan says that for one who has not understood the errors (viparyāsa), the aggregates, the entities of coming and going, are dependent or caused; 'not understood' qualifies the person, not the misconceptions.

fix.find: The entities of the aggregates, which are the coming and going of unlearned misconceptions, are what are dependent or caused.
fix.replace: For one who has not understood the errors, the entities of coming and going, namely the aggregates, are dependent or caused.

note: The MMK 25 verses and the commentary are sound; one commentary sentence is garbled.

errors.english: This famine lasts for a year, a month, and seven days.
errors.why: The famine lasts seven years, seven months and seven days ('bdun' governs all three), as in the Abhidharmakośa account.

fix.find: This famine lasts for a year, a month, and seven days.
fix.replace: This famine lasts for seven years, seven months, and seven days.

errors.english: of the period of the abiding of those who are attached
errors.why: ཆགས་པ here is cosmological 'formed' (vivṛtta), i.e. the first intermediate aeon of the abiding of the formed world, not 'those who are attached'.

fix.find: of the period of the abiding of those who are attached
fix.replace: of the period of abiding of the formed world

errors.english: They search through houses with the tips of sticks for any small bit of food.
errors.why: This is the 'famine of the sticks' (śalākā): households ration food by tally sticks, 'today the householder eats, tomorrow the housewife', not a search for scraps.

note: Generally follows the Kośa cosmology, but the famine length is wrong and the phrase for the abiding of the formed world is misread.

errors.english: Thus, the elder brother [note: the elder brother of the Brahmin Kapila], acting as a devoted friend,
errors.why: དང་པོར་སྐྱེས་པ renders Skt. agrajanman/agraja, 'brahmin' (the 'first-born' caste), not an elder brother, and the brahmin is no relative of Kapila.

fix.find: Thus, the elder brother [note: the elder brother of the Brahmin Kapila], acting as a devoted friend,
fix.replace: Thus the brahmin (agrajanman), having encouraged his dear friend,

errors.english: he saw a woman named (Bhadra) The Good One
errors.why: The girl he saw is the daughter of the brahmin Kapila (Skt. kapilasyāgrajanmanaḥ kanyām), which the English drops.

fix.find: he saw a woman named (Bhadra) The Good One
fix.replace: he saw the daughter of the brahmin Kapila, named (Bhadra) The Good One

errors.english: The elder brother of Kapila requested her hand, offering gold as the bride-price and explaining her lineage.
errors.why: He, having stated his own (the suitor's) lineage, asked Kapila (the girl's father) for her with gold as bride-price; Kapila is the one asked, not the asker's brother.

fix.find: The elder brother of Kapila requested her hand, offering gold as the bride-price and explaining her lineage.
fix.replace: Having stated his lineage, he asked Kapila for her hand, offering gold as the bride-price.

errors.english: [note: the future wife of the Brahmin Kapila]
errors.why: The proclamation is that the image is 'to be worshipped by maidens' (kanyāpūjyam) in general, and Bhadrā is Kapila's daughter, not his future wife.

note: The narrative line is followed, but the misreading of agrajanman as 'elder brother' and of Kapila's role garbles who is who in the betrothal.

errors.why: The standard logical term prayatnānantarīyaka means 'arising immediately upon effort', not 'after being sought'.

note: A difficult pramāṇa passage rendered with the argument structure intact; one standard term mistranslated.

errors.english: (Arya Manjushri-vikurvana Sutra) The Noble Sutra of the Manifestations of Manjushri
errors.why: འཇམ་དཔལ་རྣམ་པར་རོལ་པ is the Mañjuśrīvikrīḍita ('Play of Mañjuśrī'), not a vikurvaṇa ('manifestations') sūtra.

note: A faithful rendering of the Śikṣāsamuccaya citations from the Ratnakūṭa and the Sarvāstivāda Vinaya; only the sūtra title is off.
The apoha argument about unrelatedness and exclusion as the basis of universals is rendered accurately.

errors.english: If the Teacher, who knows all beings without exception, perceives emptiness,
errors.why: The phrase means 'when [the world] is seen to be empty of the Teacher who knows all beings', i.e. after his passing; the Teacher is not the one who perceives emptiness.

fix.find: If the Teacher, who knows all beings without exception, perceives emptiness,
fix.replace: When the world is seen to be empty of the Teacher, who knows all beings without exception,

errors.why: With བླ་ན་ from the previous side this is 'unsurpassed (anuttara) benefit', not 'selfless'.

note: The glosses on the four truths are sound, but two epithets are misconstrued, one of them inverting who sees the world empty.

errors.english: The sixty-first leaf chapter from the Vine of the Bodhisattva's Heroic Deeds (Bodhisattvavadanakalpalata), being the account of the Farmer (Karshaka).
errors.why: This is the closing colophon of chapter 61 (the Farmer), and what follows begins the next avadāna; the English turns it into a heading, so the Suprabuddha story reads as the Farmer's account.

fix.find: The sixty-first leaf chapter from the Vine of the Bodhisattva's Heroic Deeds (Bodhisattvavadanakalpalata), being the account of the Farmer (Karshaka).
fix.replace: Thus ends the account of the Farmer (Karshaka), the sixty-first leaf of the Vine of the Bodhisattva's Heroic Deeds (Bodhisattvavadanakalpalata). [The next chapter begins.]

note: The verses are rendered acceptably, but the chapter colophon is mistaken for the title of the following story.

errors.english: because the basis lacks differentiation, the reason lacks an established substrate
errors.why: The point is that the particular substrate is not established, so the reason is āśrayāsiddha; 'the basis lacks differentiation' misreads རྟེན་ཁྱད་པར་.

fix.find: because the basis lacks differentiation, the reason lacks an established substrate
fix.replace: because the specific substrate is not established, the reason has an unestablished substrate (āśrayāsiddha)

errors.english: Does one intend to establish speech itself autonomously
errors.why: The reason under discussion is 'being an occasional speaker' (རེས་འགའ་), which the English reduces to 'speech itself'.

note: The argument structure of the svatantra/prasaṅga dilemma and the smoke-fire objection is clear; one logical term is misread.
